newsitem.title: UK: ITT bid for Ladbroke seen as unlikely.
newsitem.headline: ITT bid for Ladbroke seen as unlikely.

text.p: A bid from ITT Corp for British betting and hotel company Ladbroke Group Plc was labelled unlikely on Monday by share analysts.
"I wouldn't give too much credence to it," said Greg Feehely of Dresdner Kleinwort Benson.

Press speculation has surfaced in Britain that ITT, the Sheraton hotels and Caesar's World casino group, could bid for Ladbroke as part of its defence against a $6.5 billion bid by Hilton Hotels Corp (HHC).
HHC and Ladbroke last month sealed a worldwide alliance to reunite the Hilton hotel brand for the first time in 32 years.
HHC owns the rights to the Hilton brand in the U.S. while Ladbroke holds them in the rest of the world.
"Either way the ITT/Hilton situation is good news for Ladbroke shareholders," added Feehely.

He said the renewed bid speculation would support the Ladbroke share price. Ladbroke also stands to gain a number of new management contracts for non-U.S. Sheraton hotels if the HHC bid proves successful.
Ladbroke shares put on 3.5p to 232.5p on Monday morning.
The speculation was fuelled by news that Ladbroke chief executive Peter George had talks with ITT 12 months ago.
Documents filed to the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission last week said the two groups discussed a possible joint venture or merger.
"Peter George was approached in February last year by ITT. There were preliminary discussions but they came to nothing," a Ladbroke spokesman said.
Other London-based share analysts said it would be wrong to read too much into the disclosure.
"People from companies in the same industry talk to each other all the time. I suspect that was all there was to it in this case," said one.
